title: Chargeback Holdback on Northloop Payments On-Demand Payouts
content:
**Rule.** Northloop keeps back a chargeback holdback from a Northloop Payments on-demand payout. The chargeback holdback is the chargeback debits booked in the last six months less the debits returned on won disputes in those six months, never below zero, times a chargeback holdback share of 1.0 when at least 3 chargebacks were debited in the last six months, 0.5 when 1 or 2 were debited, and 0 when none was, rounded to the cent.

It is deducted from the on-demand payable amount together with any other holdback kept back from the payout; the on-demand payout so obtained is never below zero, is capped at the plan's maximum per payout and is rounded to the cent. What is kept back stays in the balance and is paid with later scheduled payouts.

A window of the last six months takes in the ledger entries dated after the same calendar day six months before the request date, up to and including the request date.

## Share by count

| Chargebacks debited to the account in the last six months | Chargeback holdback share |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 1.0 |
| 1 or 2 | 0.5 |
| none | 0 |

## Hypothetical worked examples

- Three chargeback debits in the window totalling 900.00 USD, of which 300.00 USD was returned on a won dispute in the window: the net is 600.00 USD; share 1.0; holdback 600.00 USD.
- Two chargeback debits totalling 400.00 USD, nothing returned: net 400.00 USD; share 0.5; holdback 200.00 USD.
- One chargeback debit of 250.00 USD, returned in full on a won dispute: the net is 0.00, so the holdback is 0.00 USD whatever the share.
